chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, son of Yahya, from Abdullah, son of Muhammad, son of Isa, from his father, from Abdullah, son of Al-Mughira, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Prayer is a scale; whoever fulfills it, will be fulfilled (with reward).'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of prayer as a scale on the Day of Judgment in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, the Prophet (SAWW) metaphorically defines prayer as a 'scale' (Mizan), emphasizing that its spiritual weight determines one's ultimate fate. Shia scholars interpret 'Wafa' (fulfillment) not merely as ritual completion, but as the precise adherence to both outward conditions and inward presence of heart, ensuring the believer receives their full due reward without diminution. This concept underscores the centrality of Salat as the primary metric for evaluating a believer's devotion in the eschatological accounting.
